statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-55200: ssh2_transport_read() in src/transport.c did not enforce an upper bound on packet_length, so a crafted packet could corrupt heap memory. It is fixed upstream by https://github.com/libssh2/libssh2/commit/97acf3dfda80c91c3a8c9f2372546301d4a1a7a8 (https://github.com/libssh2/libssh2/pull/2052), and Alpine lists it as fixed in 1.11.1-r3 in the secfixes of its libssh2 recipe (https://gitlab.alpinelinux.org/alpine/aports/-/blob/3.23-stable/main/libssh2/APKBUILD). We checked every published libssh2 build for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository, 1.11.1-r1 to 1.11.1-r5, on x86_64 and aarch64, each verified against its index checksum: the shared library /usr/lib/libssh2.so.1.0.1 (libssh2) and the static library /usr/lib/libssh2.a (libssh2-static), with function boundaries taken from the libssh2-dbg debug symbols and from the static library's symbol table. The fix adds a comparison of packet_length against LIBSSH2_PACKET_MAXPAYLOAD (40000). In the static library's _libssh2_transport_read(), the number of comparisons against 40000 rises from two in 1.11.1-r1 and 1.11.1-r2 to three in every build from 1.11.1-r3 on, on both architectures. 1.11.1-r3 is the first fixed build, and every later build carries the fix.

CVE-2026-55200: in libssh2 1.11.0 and 1.11.1, _libssh2_transport_read() (src/transport.c) does not check packet_length against LIBSSH2_PACKET_MAXPAYLOAD on the path that reads a whole packet before decrypting it, so a crafted packet length from a malicious server can lead to an out-of-bounds heap write. It is fixed upstream by https://github.com/libssh2/libssh2/commit/97acf3dfda80c91c3a8c9f2372546301d4a1a7a8 (https://github.com/libssh2/libssh2/pull/2052), which adds that check. Two builds of this owner are published in the DHI Alpine 3.24 repository, 1.96.0-r0 and 1.96.1-r0, each as the rust and cargo packages for x86_64 and aarch64; all eight packages were unpacked and every ELF file in them was searched for libssh2 code. In 1.96.0-r0, /usr/bin/cargo has libssh2 compiled in statically through the libssh2-sys 0.3.1 crate, which bundles the libssh2 1.11.1 release (commit a312b43): the program carries the banner SSH-2.0-libssh2_1.11.1_DEV, does not list libssh2.so.1 among its needed libraries, and contains error messages from libssh2's src/packet.c and src/transport.c. The src/transport.c in libssh2-sys 0.3.1 (https://crates.io/crates/libssh2-sys/0.3.1) lacks the check the fix adds on that path, and transport.c is compiled into cargo (its messages Failed to calculate MAC and Unable to get random bytes for packet padding are present), so 1.96.0-r0 is affected. In 1.96.1-r0, cargo is linked against the system libssh2 instead (it needs libssh2.so.1, supplied by the separate libssh2 package) and contains no copy of libssh2: neither the banner nor any of the src/packet.c or src/transport.c messages found in 1.96.0-r0 is present. Alpine made that change in its rust 1.96.1-r0 recipe and lists this CVE as fixed there: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/commit/0f7dfa74845f47bc7ae7251e07fd7d68716870b8. The rust package of both builds contains no libssh2 code. 1.96.1-r0 is the first build of this owner without the vulnerable code.

CVE-2026-55200: ssh2_transport_read() in src/transport.c did not enforce an upper bound on packet_length, so a crafted packet could corrupt heap memory. It is fixed upstream by https://github.com/libssh2/libssh2/commit/97acf3dfda80c91c3a8c9f2372546301d4a1a7a8 (https://github.com/libssh2/libssh2/pull/2052). Debian fixed it for trixie in 1.11.1-1+deb13u1 (DSA-6365-1, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-55200). We checked every published libssh2 build for Debian 13 based on 1.11.1-1+deb13u1 or later in the DHI Debian repository, on amd64 and arm64, each verified against its index checksum: the shared library libssh2.so.1.0.1 (libssh2-1t64), the static library libssh2.a (libssh2-1-dev) and the libssh2-1t64-dbgsym debug symbols. Each build's Debian changelog includes the 1.11.1-1+deb13u1 security update entry naming this CVE. The fix adds a comparison of packet_length against LIBSSH2_PACKET_MAXPAYLOAD (40000); the static library's _libssh2_transport_read() contains five comparisons against 40000 in each of these builds, one more than a build of Debian's unfixed 1.11.1-1, on both architectures. The range's fixed version is the first DHI build of 1.11.1-1+deb13u1, and every later build carries the fix.
